issue.title: bazel crashes when using select() with the pure attribute
issue.body:
I'm using bazel version 0.22.0 and rules_go version 0.16.6.

I've set up a custom `CROSSTOOL` to be able to cross-compile cgo for other linux architectures besides amd64.

The `pure = "auto"` setting disables cgo whenever one is cross-compiling, so I attempted to use a `select()` to enable this only when targeting linux:

```python
 go_binary(
    name = "kubelet",
    embed = [":go_default_library"],
    pure = select({
        "@io_bazel_rules_go//go/platform:linux": "off",
        "//conditions:default": "auto",
    }),
    x_defs = version_x_defs(),
)
```

issue.body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind cleanup

**What this PR does / why we need it**: basic proof-of-concept support for cross-compilation using Bazel.

Cross compiling linux-to-linux seems to work, with the caveat that one needs to have the `crossbuild-essential` debian packages installed or run this inside docker. (Using `build/run.sh` won't work, at least not yet, since the `kube-cross` image doesn't have Bazel, and generated files aren't included in the build container and Bazel doesn't produce all of them yet.)

Cross-compiling to macOS and windows works without using any custom crosstool chain, since we don't cross-compile any cgo. Because of https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/5120 we have to use a somewhat roundabout workaround, since we can't use a select with the `pure` attribute like we'd prefer.

Most of the changes here are not actually cgo-specific; there's a lot of work just configuring groups to only include targets appropriate for the specified platform.

An example cross-compilation to linux/arm looks like
```
bazel build --config=cross:linux_arm //cmd/kubectl
```

body: Any idea if or when this might be fixed? We had to resort to a [somewhat ugly workaround](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/81e7858ece4713e043d61d96874481134c77b086/build/go.bzl#L17-L52), and it'd be nice if this worked more like we'd expect.

I have a pending change that turns the crash into a proper error. So strictly speaking it'll fix this bug.

But I understand there's also the desire to properly support aspect parameters + select(). That's unfortunately more involved since aspect definitions read their attributes values in places before it's possible to know what the select() will resolve to. So it'll take a deeper refactoring of aspects to make that work. I'm going to consider that a separate issue.

issue.body:
### Description of the problem / feature request:

When an aspect declares  `attrs = {foo:...}`, the build fails when the rule it's attached to sets `foo = select(...)`:

```
ERROR: /home/workspace/BUILD:3:1: //:hello: attribute 'pure' has a select() and aspect 
//:def.bzl%go_archive_aspect also declares '//:hello'. Aspect attributes don't currently
support select().
```

Before my fix to #5120, this was a crash. My fix turned it into a proper error. But there's no conceptual reason why this shouldn't work.

### Feature requests: what underlying problem are you trying to solve with this feature?

Reduce instances where rule users can't use `select()` for no clear reason.

### Bugs: what's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.

Copied from #5120:

```
# BUILD.bazel

load("//:def.bzl", "go_binary")

go_binary(
    name = "hello",
    srcs = ["hello.go"],
    pure = select({"//conditions:default": "auto"}),
)
```
```
# def.bzl

def _go_archive_aspect_impl(ctx):
  return []

go_archive_aspect = aspect(
    _go_archive_aspect_impl,
    attrs = {
        "pure": attr.string(values = [
            "on",
            "off",
            "auto",
        ]),
    },
)

def _go_binary_impl(ctx):
  return []

go_binary = rule(
    _go_binary_impl,
    attrs = {
        "srcs": attr.label_list(allow_files = [".go"]),
        "deps": attr.label_list(aspects = [go_archive_aspect]),
        "pure": attr.string(
            values = [
                "on",
                "off",
                "auto",
            ],
            default = "auto",
        ),
    },
)
```

### What operating system are you running Bazel on?

Linux.

### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

`release 0.23.2`

### What's the output of `git remote get-url origin ; git rev-parse master ; git rev-parse HEAD` ?

https://github.com/gregestren/bazel.git
52cf982bfad2836f7b7239a67ee322d90f43c4d5
21d03fed6f78ad3473e4f83d83e1a33b18119b69

###  Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

Just #5120.

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

While conceptually simple, this won't be a 10-minute fix.

The problem is that aspect definitions are created during Bazel's *loading* phase, which is before Bazel knows what values `select()s` actually bind to. And aspect definitions read their attribute values as a part of initialization.

So to fix this we have to refactor aspect definitions to either **a)** not read their attribute values or **b)** read them in some lazy way that can be deferred until the aspect implementation triggers.
